quest.name: The Ashen Penitent
quest.text: Peace, wanderer. Peace... though you have known little of it.

I am Brother Ashen. I keep the candles for souls that were cut short - and lately, too many of them carry your name. I do not judge you. I only ask: will you walk the Ashen Road? Four candles burn for the slain in the wild places. Kneel at each and pray, and their weight may lift from you. But hear the vow: until the last candle is lit, you will raise your hand against no one, and you will not fall.
The first candle burns not far from here; your radar will guide you. When you reach it, sit and pray. The slain may come to test you - lay them to rest first. And remember the vow.
Walk the Ashen Road. Your radar shows the first candle.
The faces of the slain gather around the flame...
The slain will not hear your prayer while they walk. Lay them to rest.
The candle flares. One name grows quiet.
Another candle calls. Follow your radar.
You raised your hand again. The candles gutter out.
You fell on the Ashen Road. The candles gutter out.
Go gently.
The candles will wait. So will I.
I will light a candle for you anyway.
Then I will pray for them alone.
Four candles burn steady. The names are quieter now - not forgotten, but quieter. Your stain is washed away. Go, and carry less than you did.
Walk lighter, friend.

quest.name: Crown of Blood

echo.name: Echo of Sir Aldric the Unyielding
echo.line: A thousand duels, and you still think steel is enough?

echo.name: Echo of Mirra Quickblade
echo.line: Keep up, if you can.

echo.name: Echo of Grond the Twice-Born
echo.line: Cut me down. I dare you.

echo.name: Echo of Valdis, the Last Duelist
echo.line: And now... me.

quest.text: So. The one whose name is whispered in every arena.

I am Valdis - or what is left of him. Once I was the last duelist standing in Aden, and the blood of a thousand rivals crowned me. You have walked that same road. The dead duelists remember you, as they remember me, and they want to know if you are worthy of the crown. Face their echoes - four of them, one after another, here and now. Leave the circle and you forfeit.
Stand where you are. They will come to you, one by one. Each fought in their own way. Learn it, or fall.
Sir Aldric cannot be harmed while his wards stand!
Every breath you hold, I take back.
You fled the circle. The crown waits for someone braver.
Then begin.
The dead are patient.
Another time, champion.
Then the crown stays with the dead.
The echoes bow. The Crown of Blood is yours - and its weight, too. Wear it well.
Until we meet in the arena beyond.

quest.name: Grudge of the Horde
quest.text: Hrr. You. You smell of orc blood.

I am Ugrash, cast out of my tribe for speaking against the Warlord. Listen, man-thing - no, listen. You have killed many of my kin. I do not weep for them; they followed Grukk. But Grukk has noticed you. He swore a blood-grudge, and his avengers are already on your trail. You cannot hide from it. But you can end it. Let them come. Break them. And when Grukk himself comes for you - and he will - put him in the ground.
Go about your hunt. They will find you - three times. Then he comes. In towns they will not dare; outside, they will.
The hunt is on - and you are the prey.
War drums, somewhere close...
Grukk's avengers!
The avengers fall. The drums go quiet... for now.
The ground shakes. Grukk is coming.
You! The one who wears my warriors' blood!
Warlord Grukk has found you!
Run all you like. Grukk always finds his prey!
Go. Be strong.
Hrr. The grudge will not wait forever.
Hrr. Deaf, like Grukk.
Then Grukk will find you anyway. Ha.
Grukk is dead? Then the grudge dies with him, and my tribe can choose a new path. My people owe you, man-thing. Take this.
Strong. Very strong. Ha!

quest.name: Death's Ledger
quest.text: Ah. There you are. Again.

Mortis, clerk of the Reaper, at your service. Do you know how many times I have written your name in the Ledger? Too many. And every time, you slipped back out. Each return tore off a sliver of your soul, and those slivers drift through the world as wisps - lonely, lost and frankly cluttering my books. Gather five of them before they fade and I shall balance your account. Be warned: the Reaper's hounds do not like to see a soul taken back.
The wisps drift away from those who chase them, so be quick and cut them off. Your radar shows where they flicker. Two may fade; no more.
Find the wisps of your soul. Your radar will show them.
A pale wisp flickers nearby. Your radar marks it.
...warm... I remember being warm...
The Reaper's hounds come to claim it back!
...too late...
A wisp faded away. Another will surface.
Too many slivers lost. The Ledger stays unbalanced.
You died. Again. The Ledger notes it.
Do hurry. Wisps are terribly unpunctual.
I will pencil you in.
I will make a note of that.
Very well. I shall keep the account open. Indefinitely.
Five slivers, returned. The account balances - for now. Do try not to die so often; my quill is wearing thin.
Until our next... appointment.

quest.name: The Lone Wolf
quest.text: You walk alone. Like us.

I am Silverfang, mother of the last free pack. I have watched you hunt - always alone, always enough. Tonight is the Hunt of the Moon: men with nets and spears come for my den and my cubs. My pack is gone. I have no one... but perhaps a lone wolf would stand with a lone wolf. Guard the den stone until the moon sets. When their Huntmaster shows himself, end him.
Here is the den stone. Stay by it. Every hand they lay on it weakens the den - drive them off.
Guard the den stone until the moon sets.
Den
The cubs whimper beneath the stone.
Moon Hunters close in on the den!
Huntmaster Vrell steps out of the dark!
Step aside. That pelt is worth a fortune.
The den is undefended! Go back!
The hunters broke into the den.
You fell, and the hunters walked over you to the den.
Run with me.
The moon will rise again.
*The wolf slips back into the trees.*
*The wolf turns away and does not look back.*
The moon sets, and the cubs sleep. You are no longer a lone wolf - you are pack. Take one of my cubs' cousins; he will follow you anywhere.
Run with us, someday.

quest.name: Nightwatch
quest.text: Oi! You there - a night-walker, aren't you? I can always tell.

Ivo's the name. Lamplighter, thirty years. The shades have been getting bolder - they snuff my lamps faster than I can light them, and tonight they're out in force. You hunt in the dark like it's nothing, so maybe you'll walk with an old man? Five lamps on my round. I light them, you keep the shades off me while the flame catches. If they swarm me, the flame goes out - and so does the road.
I'll follow you. Get me to each lamp on your radar and I'll do the rest. Keep them off me while I work!
Lead Ivo to the first lamp on your radar.
Right behind you, friend. Mind the dark.
Here's one! Hold them off while I coax the flame...
The shades swarm toward Ivo!
Shades still about! Clear them before we move!
There - she's burning bright. On to the next!
Burning Bright
Lead Ivo to the next lamp.
Flame
Ivo calls out for you in the dark!
The shades snuffed Ivo's flame.
You left Ivo alone in the dark.
Lead on, then. I'll catch up.
I'll be out every night. Find me.
Suit yourself. Mind the dark.
Fine, fine. I'll manage. I always do.
Five lamps, burning bright. The road's safe tonight, thanks to you. Here - a lamplighter's thanks, and a name for the night.
Mind the dark, Nightwatch.

quest.name: The Crownless King
quest.text: Hear me, kingslayer.

I am the herald of a king who has no crown and no kingdom - only pride. My liege has watched you topple his kind: great lords of the land, one after another. He calls it insolence. He calls it a challenge. His remnants will test you first. Then he will come himself, and he will not die easily. If you defeat him, his hoard is yours.
Do not seek him. He will seek you. Survive his remnants, then face the King - and if he runs, follow him to his hall.
The Crownless King's remnants are coming for you.
Banners on the horizon...
The King's remnants attack!
The remnants fall. Their king will not be pleased.
A herald's horn sounds. The King is coming.
Kneel, and I may let you keep your head.
The Crownless King has come!
A king does not let his quarry walk away.
Enough! To my hall!
The King retreats to his hall! Follow your radar before his wounds close.
Here, in my hall, I am still king!
The King will be... delighted.
His Majesty is not accustomed to waiting.
I shall tell His Majesty you were busy.
His Majesty will consider that a surrender.
The Crownless King has fallen at last. As promised, his hoard is yours, kingslayer.
Long live... no one.

quest.name: Bounty of the Lawless
quest.text: Ha. I know that look. You hunt the hunters.

Name's Garrick. I chased murderers for forty years before my knees gave out. You've been doing my old job - putting down the ones with blood on their names. Here's what you don't know: those killers are supplied by a bandit lord who moves his coin and orders through couriers. Three of them are on the road today. Catch them before they reach the hideout, and we cut his network at the knees.
Your radar follows each courier. They walk; you run. Don't let more than one slip through.
Watch your radar for the first courier.
A courier is on the road! Your radar marks him.
The courier made it to the hideout! Don't let the next one through.
Courier down.
Too many couriers got through. The network holds.
Good hunting.
They'll be back on the road. They always are.
Kids these days.
Your call. Bandits'll thank you.
Three couriers, three satchels of letters. With these, the bandit lord's whole network unravels. You'd have made a fine bounty hunter. Here - that's yours now.
Good hunting, Bounty Hunter.

quest.name: The Cartographer's Last Map

landmark.name: Ivory Tower
landmark.riddle: Where wizards climb toward the stars but never leave their pale home, stand at its foot.
landmark.hint: The tower of the magi, between Oren and Aden.

landmark.name: Cruma Tower
landmark.riddle: An old tower sinks into the marsh; in its halls the machines still remember their makers. Stand at its door.

landmark.name: Giran Harbor
landmark.riddle: Where ships unload the riches of the world for the richest town of the kingdom.

landmark.name: Singing Waterfall
landmark.riddle: On the island where every journey begins, the water sings as it falls.

landmark.name: Valley of Saints
landmark.riddle: Holy men were laid to rest in a valley where stone angels still keep watch, not far from the town of the wind.

landmark.name: Forest of Mirrors
landmark.riddle: A forest where every tree shows you a stranger wearing your face.

landmark.name: Frozen Waterfall
landmark.riddle: A river that stopped in the middle of its fall, in the frozen north.

landmark.name: Garden of Eva
landmark.riddle: The water goddess keeps a garden under the sea. Stand at its gate.

landmark.name: Anghel Waterfall
landmark.riddle: A waterfall named for the angels, far east of the capital.
landmark.hint: East of Aden, past the Forest of Mirrors.

landmark.name: Altar of Rites
landmark.riddle: An old altar in the elves' woods where the young once proved themselves.
landmark.hint: North of Gludio, in the Windawood.

quest.text: Ah... a traveller. A real one. I can tell by your boots.

I am Ysolde, and I drew the maps your merchants still sell. My last map was never finished: three places I could never find again, written only as riddles in my old hand. My eyes are too weak now. You have walked every road in this kingdom - you might know the places I mean. Stand where each riddle points, and my map will be whole.

Here is the first riddle. Read it again any time with the question mark. If a riddle stumps you for long, my map will begin to show you the way. Teleport, walk, swim - however you like. Dying will not stop you.
Yes... yes! Just as I drew it, long ago.
The map shifts. Another riddle appears.
A faint mark appears on your map...
Bring my map home.
The map has waited forty years. It can wait a little more.
Perhaps another traveller, then.
Then my map dies with me.
My map is whole again. I can rest. Take this - and the title of a fellow cartographer.
May every road you take lead somewhere worth going.

quest.name: The Gilded Curse
quest.text: Gold. I smell so much gold on you.

Do not be afraid. I am only a ghost - a merchant who loved gold more than life, and kept it after. Now I cannot spend it, cannot carry it, cannot let it go. You carry a fortune too; you understand. My mule is loaded with my last treasure. Lead her to the five waystones where I made my offerings, and stand guard while she rests - every bandit for leagues can smell that gold. If they rob her, my curse stays. If not... well, a little gold rubs off on whoever helps.
She'll follow you. Get her to each waystone on your radar and keep the bandits' hands off her packs.
Lead the mule to the first waystone on your radar.
*The mule snorts and falls in behind you, packs jingling.*
*The mule stops by the waystone to rest. Bandits converge!*
Bandits go for the gold!
Bandits still lurking! Drive them off!
*The mule shakes her packs, ready to go.*
Offering Made
Lead the mule to the next waystone.
Gold
The mule is alone with the gold!
The bandits stripped the mule's packs bare.
You left the mule - and the gold - behind.
Mind the packs. Every coin.
Gold can wait. Gold always waits.
You will regret walking away from gold. I did.
Then may your gold weigh on you as mine did.
Every coin offered at last. The curse is lifted... and look: the gold has left its mark on you. It suits you.
Spend it. Spend it all. Trust me.

quest.name: The Unbroken

echo.name: You, Who Never Fell
echo.line: I am what you would be, if you never had to try.

echo.name: You, Who Never Doubted
echo.line: Doubt is a door. I walked through it.

echo.name: You, Who Never Rested
echo.line: I never stop. Can you?

echo.name: You, Who Never Broke
echo.line: Break me, then. Try.

quest.text: Do you recognise me? You will.

I am you - the you of some tomorrow. You have climbed so far without falling once. Do you know how rare that is? It has made you something the world did not expect, and the world will test it. Better I test it first. Face four shadows of who you might become. Beat them, and you stay unbroken.
They come one at a time, right here. Do not leave this place. Do not fall.
Every breath you take to rest, I take too.
You ran from yourself. That never works.
So you can break after all. Get up. Try again another day.
Show me.
I know where you will be. I always do.
Funny. I remember walking away, too.
Then I will become someone else.
You beat every version of yourself. Good. Stay unbroken - for both of us.
See you tomorrow.

quest.name: The Gravedigger's Debt
quest.text: You've a grave-smell on you, friend. Don't take it wrong.

Hollis. I dig the graves round these parts, and I've dug more this year than in the twenty before. You've been sending the walking dead back where they belong - I've noticed; they come in quieter. But four old graves won't stay shut. Something keeps pulling the dead back up. Go to each grave, put down whatever climbs out, and say the old words over it. Sit and pray, quiet-like. That seals it.
First grave's on your radar. They'll climb out when you get close. Put them down, then kneel and pray.
Find the first restless grave on your radar.
The earth heaves. The dead climb out!
The grave won't settle while its dead still walk. Put them down.
The grave settles. Silence.
Another grave stirs. Follow your radar.
Mind your step out there.
The dead aren't going anywhere. Well. They are. That's the problem.
Busy, eh? So are the dead.
I'll fetch a bigger shovel, then.
Four graves, sealed. I'll sleep tonight for the first time in a month. Here - I owe you.
Rest easy. You've earned it.

quest.name: The Old Banner
quest.text: Soldier. Stand easy.

Commander Brenna, of a regiment no one remembers. You have won glory on the fields where we bled - I can see it on you. Every year on this day the phantom army of the old war rises to take our banner. Every year there are fewer of us to hold it. This year there is only me... and maybe you. Plant the banner with me and hold it until the phantoms break.
The banner stands. Hold this ground. If the phantoms touch it, it weakens - don't let them.
Hold the banner until the phantom army breaks.
Banner
The old banner snaps in a wind that isn't there.
Phantom soldiers advance on the banner!
The Phantom Siege Lord takes the field!
That rag has flown long enough.
The banner stands alone! Back to it!
The phantoms tore the banner down.
Regiment, form up!
The phantoms rise every year. I'll find you before the next.
Dismissed, then.
Then the regiment ends with me.
The banner holds - one more year. The regiment lives as long as someone remembers. Carry it with you, banner-bearer.
Regiment! Salute!

quest.name: The Laurel of Ash

echo.name: Echo of Theron, First Laurel
echo.line: The first Hero of Aden salutes you. Now defend yourself.

echo.name: Echo of Lysa the Untouched
echo.line: Nobody ever landed a blow on me in the Coliseum. Try.

echo.name: Echo of Brother Kass
echo.line: Patience wins more matches than strength.

echo.name: Echo of the Nameless Champion
echo.line: They chiselled my name off the monument. Let us see if yours deserves to stay.

quest.text: Thirty times the crowd has roared for you. I counted.

Once my name was carved on the Hero monument in Aden. Then a new season came, and a new Hero, and the stonemason took his chisel to me. That is the Olympiad: glory, then ash. Still, I watch every match, and you fight like the old champions did. Face the echoes of the Heroes who came before you - four of them, here and now, with no manager to stop the match. Win, and I will give you the laurel they took from me.
No stadium, no crowd, one rule: stay in the circle. They come one after another.
The old Heroes step out of the ash.
Brother Kass raises his wards. Break them!
The ash always settles back on me.
You left the circle. In the Coliseum, that is a forfeit.
The match is over. The laurel stays in the ash.
Begin the match.
The season is long. I will wait.
Even Heroes need rest. Another day.
Then the laurel crumbles with me.
Four Heroes, and you stand over all of them. Take the laurel. They may chisel your name off the stone someday - but not this.
May the crowd always remember your name.

quest.name: The Smith's Lament
quest.text: Ah. There you are. I heard you from across the kingdom.

Borin Ashforge, master of the Black Anvil, dead these hundred years. Every time a blade breaks under a scroll, I hear it - a little scream in the metal. And I have heard YOU, friend, over and over. Broken steel does not rest. The shards gather, the rust wakes, and it all crawls back looking for whoever broke it. Let me set up my old anvil here. I will reforge the souls of what you lost, and you keep the rust off me until the work is done.
The anvil is down. Stand by it. Whatever crawls out of the rust wants to smash it - every blow they land is a blow I lose.
Guard the anvil until Borin finishes the reforging.
Forge
*Clang. Clang. Clang.* The anvil rings with every lost blade.
Rustborn crawl out of the scrap!
The Slag King rises from the broken steel!
Everything you broke... is ME.
The anvil is unguarded! Back to the forge!
The Rustborn smashed the anvil. The reforging is ruined.
You fell, and the rust buried the anvil.
Bellows! Hammer! Let's work.
I'll keep the coals warm.
Hmph. I'll listen for the next one breaking, then.
Then your broken steel can haunt you instead of me.
Done! Every broken blade, reforged into something better - luck. Smith's luck. Take these; they won't fail you the way the others did. Well. Not as badly.
Strike true, and pray to the anvil.

quest.name: The One That Got Away
quest.text: You there! You've got the smell of the lake on you. Good.

Pell's the name. Fished every lake in the kingdom for sixty years, and there's one I never landed: the Silver Shadow. Not a fish, exactly - more the spirit of every fish that ever slipped the hook. Today it's come up out of the water, swimming through the air like it owns the place and splitting into silver shadows. You've landed more fish than anyone I know. Help an old man catch his legend before it dives back down - five shadows, quick, before they fade.
Your radar shows where a shadow glints. They dart off when you come close, so cut them off. And mind the poachers - they want my legend for themselves.
Find the silver shadows. Your radar will show them.
A silver shadow glints nearby. Your radar marks it.
*The shadow wriggles, flashes silver, and is caught.*
Poachers! They want the catch!
*splash*
A shadow dove back into the deep. Another will surface.
Too many got away. The Silver Shadow sinks back to the bottom.
You fell. The Silver Shadow swims off, laughing in bubbles.
Easy now. Patience and a quick hand.
The lake will still be there. So will I.
Huh. The ones that walk away are always the biggest.
Then I'll just tell the story. Nobody believes it anyway.
Five shadows! Look at it - the Silver Shadow, at last! Sixty years. Here, take this. And when people ask you about the one that got away, you tell them: not this time.
Tight lines, friend.

quest.name: The Still Mountain
quest.text: Hm. You sit well. Most people do not know how.

I am Oru. I have lived on the mountain longer than I remember, and I have watched you: resting in the open among the beasts, as calm as a stone in a stream. Few adventurers can be still. Three Stones of Stillness stand in the wild; at each, sit and empty your mind until the stone answers. Your restless thoughts will try to stop you - quiet them first. And take a vow: until the last stone, you raise your hand against no one.
The first stone is on your radar. When your thoughts rise, settle them. Then sit, and wait. Do not hurry; the stone knows.
Seek the first Stone of Stillness. Your radar shows the way.
Your restless thoughts take shape around the stone...
The stone cannot hear you over your own thoughts. Quiet them.
Sit before the stone, and be still.
You breathe out, and let the world go quiet...
The stillness breaks. Sit, and begin again.
The stone hums, low and deep. Something in you settles.
Another stone waits. Follow your radar.
You raised your hand. The stillness is gone.
You fell. Even the mountain cannot be still forever.
Go slowly.
The mountain is patient. So am I.
Ah. Not yet still enough.
Then I will sit alone. I usually do.
Three stones answered you. You carry the mountain inside you now - when the world shakes, you will not. A hermit has little to give, but this little is true.
Be still, and know.

quest.name: Dance on the Edge

echo.name: Last Breath
echo.line: One breath left. That is all anyone ever has.

echo.name: Racing Heart
echo.line: Faster now. Faster.

echo.name: Last Light
echo.line: The world gets very bright at the very end, doesn't it?

echo.name: Death's Partner
echo.line: Shall we dance?

quest.text: There you are. Still a little blood left in you, I see.

They call me Sable. I dance with Death. Most fighters run when their blood runs low - but not you. A hundred times you have stood on the edge with one breath left and struck the killing blow anyway. Death has noticed. She would like a dance, and I have offered to arrange it. Four partners, one after another, here and now. Keep your feet, don't leave the floor, and don't fall.
The floor is right here. They come one by one. You'll find you fight best when you have the least to lose. You always have.
The music starts. Your first partner steps forward.
I never tire. Do you?
You left the floor. Death does not forgive a partner who walks out.
You stepped over the edge. Get up. She will ask again.
Then dance.
The music never really stops.
Shy? You don't look shy when you're bleeding.
A pity. You would have danced beautifully.
You danced with Death and she let go of your hand. She is smiling, you know - she likes you. Take this, and keep dancing on the edge. Just not over it.
Until the next dance.

quest.name: The Empty Hand
quest.text: Your hands. Show me your hands. Yes... I thought so.

I am Tavik of the Open Palm. My school teaches that the hand is the oldest weapon and the only one you can never lose. Three hundred times you have killed with nothing in your hands, and word of that travels. It has reached the Iron Fist school, whose grandmaster, Korvash, believes there is only one way of the hand: his. His disciples will test you. When they fail, he will come himself. Beat him, and the Open Palm will call you one of its own.
Go on with your day. The disciples will find you - three times. In towns they will wait; they keep a code, of sorts. Then Korvash.
The Iron Fist school is looking for you.
Bare feet on stone, somewhere close. Disciples.
Iron Fist disciples attack!
The disciples bow, bloodied, and limp away.
A deep voice counts the beats of a kata. Korvash is coming.
An empty hand? Mine is iron.
Grandmaster Korvash has found you!
A disciple runs. A grandmaster follows.
Breathe. Open the hand.
The hand is patient.
The Iron Fist will not be as polite as I am.
Then the Iron Fist may knock on your door uninvited.
Korvash is beaten. Perhaps now he will learn what his disciples could not. Welcome to the Open Palm.
The hand remembers.

quest.name: The Drowned Choir
quest.text: You taste of salt and deep water. Hello, swimmer.

I am Nerissa, of the water. I have watched you fight where others only drown, and all that splashing has woken the drowned dead. Now they have formed a choir, and they sing a song that pulls ships down. I can sing against them with my Tide Stone, but my song is fragile. Guard the stone while I sing, and the drowned will finally rest.
The Tide Stone sings. Do not let them touch it; every drowned hand on it is a note I lose.
Guard the Tide Stone until Nerissa's song is finished.
Song
The stone hums like a shell held to the ear.
The drowned choir walks out of the mist, singing!
A great sunken bell tolls - something answers it!
Down... down... down to the quiet...
The Tide Stone is alone! Return to it!
The drowned silenced the Tide Stone.
You sank, and the choir sang on.
Then I sing.
The tide always comes back.
The sea will remember you anyway.
Then I will sing alone, as I always have.
The choir is silent. The drowned sleep at last, and ships will sail safely for a while. The sea gives you its thanks - and a little of its voice.
Swim deep, and come back up.

quest.name: The Wronged
quest.text: Don't be scared. I'm one of you. One of the... unlucky ones.

My name was Tam. I was a page carrying letters when someone killed me for the fun of it. You know how that feels - they've done it to you again and again, haven't they? The murderers on the roads aren't all lone wolves. Many are paid by the Red Hand, a guild that sells killings and buys silence. Today three of their couriers carry the list of who to kill next. Catch them before they reach their hideout. Let's take something from them for once.
Your radar follows each courier. They walk, you run. Let no more than one get away.
Watch your radar for the first Red Hand courier.
A Red Hand courier is on the road! Your radar marks him.
The courier reached the hideout. Don't let the next one through!
The courier falls. A bloody list spills from his satchel.
Too many couriers got through. The Red Hand's lists go out.
They got you again. I'm sorry. I know how it feels.
Thank you. Truly.
I'm not going anywhere. I can't.
I understand. It's hard to be brave when it keeps happening.
Then I'll keep waiting for someone else.
Three lists, three couriers. Every name on those pages will live a little longer because of you. Mine was on one, once. Take this - and walk the roads with your head high.
They can't take this from you.

quest.name: The Archivist's Burden
quest.text: You! Yes, you - I have read about you. Thirty times, in fact.

Archivist Baulden, of the Hall of Records. Every deed of note in this kingdom ends up in my books, and lately a great many of them have your name in them. But the books are hunted: the Shades of Oblivion devour whatever is written down, and they have found my archive. I must move the chronicles to four hidden vaults in the wild. Who better to guard the record of great deeds than the one who did them? Walk with me, and keep the shades off while I seal each vault.
I will follow you. Lead me to each vault on your radar and keep the shades off me while I seal it. They eat ink, but they don't mind a bit of archivist either.
Lead Baulden to the first hidden vault on your radar.
Lead on. Mind the satchel, it's heavier than it looks.
Here! Hold them off while I write the seal...
Shades of Oblivion swarm toward the chronicles!
Shades still lurking! I can't open the satchel with them about!
Sealed. Not even Oblivion will find that one. Onward!
Vault Sealed
Lead Baulden to the next vault.
Chronicle
Baulden calls out for you, clutching his satchel!
The shades devoured the chronicles. A hundred years of deeds, forgotten.
You left Baulden and the chronicles alone.
Splendid! I shall take notes.
I will make an appointment in my ledger.
Hmph. Not every deed is worth recording, I suppose.
Then I shall write that you declined. In small letters.
Four vaults, sealed. The chronicles are safe - and the last page now records how you saved them. A loremaster deserves a loremaster's reward.
I'll be reading about you, I'm sure.

quest.name: The Road Goes Ever On

landmark.name: Ruins of Agony
landmark.riddle: Where old stones still cry out in pain, a day's walk from the walls of Gludio.

landmark.name: Dragon Valley
landmark.riddle: A valley where the bones of dragons lie, and some of the bones still breathe.

landmark.name: Execution Grounds
landmark.riddle: Where the condemned walked their last road, halfway between the town of Dion and the richest town of all.

landmark.name: Sea of Spores
landmark.riddle: A sea with no water, where mushrooms taller than men breathe clouds into the air.

landmark.name: Fields of Massacre
landmark.riddle: A field where two armies met and none walked home, beyond the capital toward the rising sun.

landmark.name: Hot Springs
landmark.riddle: Where the earth is warm enough to bathe in, though the beasts there do not like to share.

landmark.name: Imperial Tomb
landmark.riddle: An emperor sleeps behind sealed doors, east of the town that watches the mountain passes.

landmark.name: Den of Evil
landmark.riddle: A den in the snow where evil things gather to keep warm.

landmark.name: Frost Lake
landmark.riddle: A lake so cold that it forgot how to move.

landmark.name: Isle of Prayer
landmark.riddle: An island where the faithful once went to be heard, across the water from the town of the water goddess.

quest.text: Well met on the road! And what a road it's been for you, eh?

Dorrin Farstride. I've worn out more boots than most dwarves have worn out beards, and I thought nobody walked farther than me. Then I saw your tracks. Everywhere. So here's a game for two wanderers: I give you riddles about places I've stood, and you go and stand there too. No hurry - teleport, walk, swim, however you like. Four riddles, and we'll know which of us is the true Far-Strider.
Here's the first riddle. Click the question mark to read it again. If a riddle stumps you for long, my old map will start to help. Dying won't stop the game.
Ha! You found it. I left my mark on that stone myself, see?
Dorrin scribbles another riddle.
A faint line appears on Dorrin's map...
Lace your boots!
The road will wait. It always does.
Off you go, then. Somewhere, I'm sure.
Then I'll keep the title. Ha!
Four for four! I bow to you, Far-Strider. The road goes ever on - and so, it seems, do you.
See you at the end of the road. If there is one.

quest.name: The Long Night
quest.text: Still standing, are you? Most don't last the night out here.

Bram. I keep the Last Fire. For forty years I've lit it on the darkest nights, so the shadows remember they don't own the dark. You've walked through five nights out here and walked out again at dawn - I've seen you. My legs are done. Sit with my fire tonight. Keep the shadows off it until the sun comes up, and you'll know what I know.

There she is - the Last Fire. Shadows will come for her all night, more of them the darker it gets. Keep them off her until dawn. And when the last of them comes - it always does - put it out before it puts her out.
Keep the Last Fire burning until dawn.
Fire
*The fire crackles and pushes back the dark.*
Night Prowlers creep toward the fire!
The Last Shadow rises against the fire!
Every fire goes out. Yours is next.
The sun is coming! Finish the Last Shadow!
The fire is alone! Go back!
The shadows smothered the Last Fire.
You fell, and the fire guttered out in the dark.
Too close to dawn for a vigil. Find me tomorrow night.
Sit close. It'll be a long one.
The nights are long. I'll find you.
Hm. Another night, then.
Then I'll keep her myself. Somehow.
Dawn - and she's still burning. You kept the Last Fire through the long night. That makes you one of us now: the ones who keep the dark honest. Take this, and the name that goes with it.
Keep a fire in you, Dawnkeeper.

quest.name: Crown of the Night

echo.name: Echo of the Ashen Nightlord
echo.line: I ruled the night you stole from me.

echo.name: Echo of the Howling Nightlord
echo.line: Catch me in the dark, if you can.

echo.name: Echo of the Hollow Nightlord
echo.line: Cut me down. There is always more night.

echo.name: Echo of the First Nightlord
echo.line: Every crown you took was mine. Kneel.

quest.text: You. The one the Nightlords whisper about.

I am the Herald of Dusk, and I serve whoever wears the Crown of the Night. Ten of its lords have fallen to you, and the dead lords will not rest until one of the living proves the crown has a new master. Their echoes will face you one by one, here, under the moon. Leave the circle, and the crown stays with the dead.
Stand your ground. They come one at a time, each as they ruled. Learn their ways, or fall before the dawn.
Stand your ground. The Nightlords' echoes are coming.
The First Nightlord cannot be harmed while his wards stand!
The night heals me. Does it heal you?
You fled the circle. The night has no master tonight.
The sun rises, and the echoes fade with the dark. The crown waits for another night.
The night is nearly over. The crown is only won in the dark.
Then let the night watch.
The crown waits for the dark.
Another night, then.
Then the crown sleeps.
The last echo kneels. The Crown of the Night is yours. Wear it when the sun goes down, and let every Nightlord that rises know who rules the dark.
Rule the dark well, Nightcrowned.

quest.name: Moonlit Waters
quest.text: The moon is in the water tonight. So are you, it seems.

I am Lunne. I sing to the moon, and on the right nights it sings back. You have fished by moonlight a hundred times; the lakes know your lures by now. Tonight the moon's reflection has slipped out of the water as a little light - a wisp - and it wants to lead someone to the Sunken Cache, where the drowned keep what the lakes took. Follow it before the sun rises. When the sun comes up, the wisp goes back into the water, and the cache with it.
There it is - see it bobbing? Stay close; it waits for you at every stop. The drowned want the cache too, and they will try to take the wisp from you.
Follow the wisp before the sun rises. Your radar shows it.
*The wisp bobs, and drifts off like moonlight on water.*
The wisp drifts on across the dark. Follow it!
Drowned thieves rise to snatch the wisp!
The wisp brightens again.
The wisp's light is fading in the distance! Follow your radar.
*The wisp sinks into the ground with a soft splash.*
The Keepers of the Deep rise around the Sunken Cache!
The keepers are gone. Go to the Sunken Cache.
*The lid lifts with a sigh of old water.*
You lost the wisp, and it slipped back into the water.
The sun rises, and the wisp slips back into the water.
You fell, and the drowned claimed the wisp.
The moon is nearly down. Find me another night.
Quietly now - wisps are shy.
The moon comes back every night. So will I.
*She hums, and turns back to the water.*
Then the cache sleeps on.
You found it - the Sunken Cache, and all the lakes kept. Take it; the moon wants it to go to someone who listens. And take these too. They shine brightest when the moon is up.
Fish by moonlight, friend.

quest.name: The Witching Bell
quest.text: You smell of grave-dirt and midnight. Good.

Sister Vespera. I hunt witches - one witch, really. Every Witching Hour, when the dead rise, a bell tolls that only the dead can hear. It is hers. You have cut down three hundred of the things it called, and the bell is angry with you. That means it is listening: tonight her will-o'-the-wisp will lead whoever it hates most to her grave. Follow the wisp, break her bellringers, and open the grave before dawn - and the bell goes silent.
The wisp is hers. It leads you to her grave because it wants you dead there. Let it. Her familiars will come at you on the way.
Follow the witch's wisp before the sun rises. Your radar shows it.
*The wisp giggles and floats away.*
The wisp floats deeper into the dark. Follow it!
The witch's familiars swarm out of the dark!
The wisp giggles and drifts on.
The wisp's giggle fades in the distance! Follow your radar.
*Somewhere, a bell tolls.*
The bellringers rise from the grave!
The bellringers are silent. Open the grave.
*The bell inside cracks, and is still.*
The wisp giggled and vanished.
The sun rises, and the grave sinks back into the earth until the next Witching Hour.
You fell, and the bell tolled for you.
Not enough night left. The bell waits for the next one.
Bless you. Bring a good weapon.
The bell will toll again tomorrow night.
Then I will hunt her alone.
So be it. May you never hear the bell.
The bell is cracked - I heard it stop. Whatever she left in that grave is yours; you have earned it more than I. And a name, for those who will hear of this.
Sleep soundly. You can, now.
